newsitem.title: FINLAND: NOKIA CEO SEES RISING FINNISH HIGH-TECH EXPORTS.
newsitem.headline: NOKIA CEO SEES RISING FINNISH HIGH-TECH EXPORTS.

text.p: Jorma Ollila, CEO of telecoms group Nokia Oy and chairman of the Finnish Foreign Trade Association, said on Thursday that Finnish high-tech exports were likely to go on outpacing high-tech imports.
The rise in the share of exports of high-technology products has been the most rapid in Finland of all OECD-countries, Ollila said in the text of a prepared speech.

"Currently it is over 12 percent, according to the OECD's new definitions," he said. "Finland has become a net exporter of technology products ... It strongly seems that this trend will continue also in years to come," Ollila said.
Such a trend would increase the significance of high-tech manufacturing for the entire Finnish economy, he said.
Ollila spoke as chairman of the foreign trade lobby at a ceremony where three high-tech firms received the Finnish President's annual export awards.
Trade and Industry Minister Antti Kalliomaki said in his prepared remarks that a strong industrial base and a dynamic economy were necessary to maintain the welfare state.
Kalliomaki referred to an OECD report and said Finland had managed to shift towards an information technology industry quicker and more flexibly than OECD countries on average.

"Production and exports of high-technology (goods) have increased more rapidly than in any other OECD-country. Finland is one of the few countries in the world where high-tech exports exceed imports," he said.
The change in the industrial structure had created thousands of new jobs, Kalliomaki said.
Each new job at a high-tech company like the three receiving this year's export awards indirectly creates 1.5-2.2 other jobs, he added.
